inline:The target fails to specify the necessary conditions and instead uses the single-repository limitation as a blanket refusal to infer, which contradicts the problem's demand to explain the specific observed distribution (1/9 vs 4/4–6/7).
The problem explicitly asks to 'account for' the 1/9 compile.py loss versus the 4/4 to 6/7 distribution in ordinarily-guarded modules. The target's core claim that 'no condition can be inferred' and that the result is merely 'a description of the mutation set' is a non-response: it does not engage with the specific asymmetry that compile.py—installed under shown-to-fail-first conditions—behaved differently from modules with ordinary guards. By treating the single-repository/author/week limitation as defeating all inference rather than as a scope restriction on generalizability, the target avoids the required analytical work of distinguishing constraint from description in this specific record.
